TRANSPORT-WILL GOVERNMENT GIVE PRIORITY TO IMPROVEMENT OF SERVICE BETWEEN MONTREAL AND MIRABEL
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, last Wednesday I asked the Minister of Supply and Services (Mr. La Salle) whether the government would give priority to the improvement of ground transportation between Mirabel and Montreal when he meets with his Quebec colleagues on November 5 next. I mentioned, Mr. Speaker, that this matter was an urgent and necessary priority and that the construction of a public transit system between Mirabel and Montreal would provide jobs.
The minister explained to me that there were other projects among his priorities but some Liberals considered rapid transit between Mirabel and Montreal more important than Place Guy Favreau. I am one of those who have always advocated public interest in that area rather than the other project.
At any rate, I would repeat for the benefit of hon. members that we want to hear the recommendations and submissions of the Quebec government, after which we will decide.
Mr. Speaker, this answer concerns me due to the indifference shown by the PQ government and during the time allotted to me I will try to show why I am concerned about the outcome of the project to make Mirabel airport a profitable operation.
Mr. Speaker, if I may 1 will refer to a statement made by municipal affairs minister Tardif, in an item published in the newspaper La Presse, who is in favour of a subway line to Laval rather than a metropolitan express system. Lie points out that the Quebec government has already done its part to connect the two airports efficiently. Mr. Tardif is of the opinion that the central government must assume responsibility for the metropolitan express system if it feels that it is a

priority. So we see exactly the attitude of the Parti Quebecois government and how indifferent it is to this project.
I have here in my hand the official report of the Debates of the National Assembly of April 27, 1977, when transport minister Lucien Lessard mentions it once again, and I quote;
It should also be remembered that it is up to the Department of Transport of the federal government to make Mirabel profitable.
Once again mention is made of the lack of interest on the part of the Quebec government in making the metropolitan express system a profitable undertaking.
Mr. Speaker, another attitude worries me even more, considering the situation in the byelection in Prevost, where the Liberal candidate, Mrs. Solange Chaput-Rolland, gave priority in her program to the development of the Mirabel airport and specifically the metropolitan express system while the PQ candidate, Mr. Harvey, was again totally indifferent to its importance.
It is a matter of showing how one must never get discouraged. You have to persist and persevere when you are in earnest about as important a matter as that on the development of the Mirabel airport. I have here, Mr. Speaker, letters dated December 11, 1974, from the Chamber of Commerce of Ville-de-Laval, asking me to continue my efforts toward achieving that objective; so I am speaking here of something that goes back five years.
I have in front of me another letter from the joint commission on urban development for Sainte-Therese centre, and this was done in co-operation with my colleagues in the region. First, the hon. members for Terrebonne (Mr. Comtois), Labelle (Mr. Dupras), and Duvernay (Mr. Demers), and myself have tried to meet with the aldermen, the city councillors, the mayors, in order to gain their support to develop this project. 1 have received a resolution from the joint commission on urban development, dated May 13, 1977, supporting hon. members' action concerning the development of this type of road transportation system.
I have here another resolution which says that Mirabel affords Montreal the opportunity to remain one of Canada's large urban centres, and which comes from eight executive presidents of the Trucking Association of Quebec Inc.; it also supports fully the development of this means of transportation between Mirabel and Montreal. I have still another resolution from the Mirabel Chamber of Commerce dated June 20, 1977, supporting this project, by unanimous approval of its members. And there is support from Rosemere, Sainte-Therese and Blainville which are all in favour of developing this metropolitan express system as a way of stopping the accumulation of huge deficits for this airport.
Here is more evidence, Mr. Speaker, and not the least; it is a statement made by the minister, Mr. Mailloux, at a weekly
October 30, 1979

luncheon at the Chamber of Commerce of Montreal which says, and I quote:
Mr. Mailloux indicated that the government of Quebec-
-the Liberal government of the time-
-expressed its general agreement with the principle of building a rapid transit system between Montreal and Mirabel, according to the main lines of the report, provided there is adequate financial participation from the various levels of governments.
Mr. Speaker, on December 5, in Montreal, the Liberal caucus of the area of Montreal met with the executive of the city of Montreal. At this joint meeting which had been organized by my colleague the hon. member for Terrebonne and myself, Mayor Drapeau emphasized for cabinet members as well as ordinary members the necessity to build a metropolitan express system to develop Mirabel airport. In view of all these testimonies, Mr. Speaker, and the indifference of the PQ government, I feel that this project should be given top priority in order to limit the deficit of the Mirabel operation. I feel also that the Minister of Supply and Services, who represents a constituency north of Montreal, should support the efforts of his colleagues of the former government to develop Mirabel airport. If the minister remains indifferent to this request, Mr. Speaker, I am sure that the voters will not soon forget it.

speakeroldname: Mr. Otto Jelinek (Parliamentary Secretary to Minister of Transport):
speakerposition: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Transport
subtopic: TRANSPORT-WILL GOVERNMENT GIVE PRIORITY TO IMPROVEMENT OF SERVICE BETWEEN MONTREAL AND MIRABEL
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, although the hon. member directed his original question to the Minister of Supply and Services (Mr. La Salle), it concerns transport and that is why I am taking the liberty as Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Transport to reply to the hon. member. I am surprised that after all the years he has been in the House he does not realize this matter concerns transport primarily.
I can assure the hon. member that indeed consultation will take place with the Quebec government, the city of Montreal, as well as other municipalities and interest groups on any matters pertaining to Mirabel and other areas in the province of Quebec, just as consultations will take place with other municipalities and cities in other parts of Canada before any decisions are made by this minister.
Adjournment Debate
Also I should like to answer the hon. member's question related to ground transportation service between Mirabel and downtown Montreal via Laval. Since the Mirabel airport opened in 1975, there have been adequate bus transportation services provided between Montreal and Mirabel. The Montreal Urban Community Transport Commission has been providing service from the CN central station to Mirabel and from Dorval to Mirabel. The Laval Transport Commission has been providing a service from the Henri-Bourassa metro station to Mirabel. This service carried 83,000 passengers in 1978, of which more than 90 per cent were Mirabel employees.
The level and the quality of service provided by these two transport commissions, the MUCTC and LTC, is very adequate, especially if we consider the actual level of patronage at Mirabel and the characteristics of the airport users who are mainly international passengers with flying time of many hours. Within the context of international travel the extra time required to travel by bus from Mirabel to Montreal, approximately 15 minutes, is minimal indeed when compared to the more than $100 million it would cost to implement a Mont-real-Mirabel highspeed rail system at this time. Therefore, the outlay of an expenditure in the area of $100 million, especially in this time of restraint, would be difficult to justify. I want to remind the hon. member of that fact. As for any service of this nature, ways of improvement are constantly the subject of examination and analysis, which is something the previous government did not take the time to do. With respect to this specific issue, I might add that provincial, municipal and federal officials are presently studying means to improve the downtown terminal.
Also the hon. member for Laval asked if it is the minister's intention, when he meets with the Quebec government, to consider that service as a priority. The hon. member may be assured that the minister recognizes the importance of an appropriate ground transportation system to Mirabel, particularly in the future, and that necessary steps will be taken in due course.
